h1: Hybrid search: BM25 full-text and vector search in one database
sub: Milvus is a hybrid search vector database with BM25 built in: raw text, dense and sparse vectors are searched, filtered and fused in one hybrid_search call, no second search engine to sync. When should you use hybrid search? Whenever queries mix exact terms with meaning.

benefits.title: BM25 built in
benefits.body: Declare a BM25 Function on a text field. Milvus builds sparse vectors on insert and scores raw-text queries; built-in analyzers tokenize English, Chinese (jieba), Arabic and Thai per field. No dual writes.

benefits.title: Sparse and dense vectors, one list
benefits.body: Error codes and SKUs match through BM25; paraphrased questions match through embeddings. Learned sparse embeddings such as SPLADE fit the same SPARSE_FLOAT_VECTOR field. One call returns one ranked list.

benefits.title: Fusion and metadata filtering
benefits.body: Fuse with RRF or a weighted ranker. Each request carries its own filter, applied before the ANN search, so tenant rules and metadata filtering run inside hybrid search rather than after it.

benefits.title: Rerank after fusion
benefits.body: Hybrid search with reranking in the same call: a model ranker (vLLM, TEI, Cohere, Voyage AI) or a Function Chain rescores the fused list before it returns.

feature_blocks.title: Microsoft: hybrid beats keyword and vector alone
feature_blocks.body: Azure AI Search tested BM25, Ada-002 vectors and RRF hybrid on four customer datasets and public benchmarks. Hybrid scored highest of the three modes on each.
bullets: Customer data, NDCG@3: keyword 40.6, vector 43.8, hybrid 48.4
Hybrid + semantic ranker on customer data: 60.1

feature_blocks.title: Anthropic: 49% fewer failed retrievals
feature_blocks.body: Across codebases, fiction, ArXiv and science papers, combining contextual embeddings with contextual BM25 cut the top-20 failure rate (1 minus recall@20).

feature_blocks.title: Research: complementary signals
feature_blocks.body: BEIR, an 18-dataset zero-shot benchmark, found BM25 a robust baseline and that dense retrievers often generalize poorly. Bruch et al. show lexical and semantic scores are complementary.

code.h2: How do I build hybrid search for RAG?
code.intro: Hybrid search with BM25 and embeddings: one BM25 Function, then a dense request and a raw-text request fused with RRF.
code.code:
from pymilvus import (MilvusClient, DataType, Function, FunctionType,
                      AnnSearchRequest, RRFRanker)

client = MilvusClient(uri="http://localhost:19530")

schema = client.create_schema()
schema.add_field("id", DataType.INT64, is_primary=True, auto_id=True)
schema.add_field("text", DataType.VARCHAR, max_length=1000, enable_analyzer=True)
schema.add_field("dense", DataType.FLOAT_VECTOR, dim=768)
schema.add_field("sparse", DataType.SPARSE_FLOAT_VECTOR)
schema.add_function(Function(name="bm25", input_field_names=["text"],
                             output_field_names=["sparse"], function_type=FunctionType.BM25))

index_params = client.prepare_index_params()
index_params.add_index("dense", index_type="AUTOINDEX", metric_type="IP")
index_params.add_index("sparse", index_type="SPARSE_INVERTED_INDEX", metric_type="BM25")
client.create_collection("docs", schema=schema, index_params=index_params)

# Insert a document before searching. embed() is your 768-dimensional model.
client.insert(collection_name="docs", data=[{
    "text": "Quiet white headphones with comfortable ear pads.",
    "dense": embed("Quiet white headphones with comfortable ear pads."),
}])

query = "white headphones, quiet and comfortable"
res = client.hybrid_search(
    collection_name="docs",
    reqs=[AnnSearchRequest([embed(query)], "dense", {}, limit=10),   # semantic
          AnnSearchRequest([query], "sparse", {}, limit=10)],        # BM25 on raw text
    ranker=RRFRanker(60),
    limit=5,
    output_fields=["text"],
)
code.note: Replace embed() with your 768-dim embedding model. Add expr="..." to either request to filter. Code requires a running server and your own embedding model; it is an example, not a benchmark.

compare.h2: Lexical search vs semantic search vs hybrid: when does BM25 beat vector search?
compare.caption: Keyword vs vector vs hybrid search by query type, NDCG@3; Microsoft Azure AI Search (BM25, Ada-002 vectors, RRF hybrid)
compare.note: Across all ten query types in the study, hybrid beat or came within 0.2 points of the better single path on nine; the exception is keyword-only queries. Adding a semantic reranker lifted every row further (keyword queries 66.9, long queries 59.4).

faqs: What is hybrid search in a vector database, and how does it work?

Three steps: BM25 and vector requests run in parallel on one collection, a ranker fuses the two lists, and the top-k returns with its fields. In Milvus that is one hybrid_search call, filters and reranking included.
Do I still need Elasticsearch for keyword search?
Not for BM25 retrieval. Milvus computes BM25 natively and searches with raw text. Keep a separate engine only for needs like log analytics or aggregations.
How does reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) work?

Each hit scores 1/(k + rank) in every list it appears in, and the scores are summed. With the default k=60 a rank-1 hit scores 1/61, so no score calibration is needed. Milvus 3.0.1+ also accepts per-path weights on RRF.
How do I tune the balance between keyword and semantic search?

Use the weighted ranker, the equivalent of a hybrid search alpha parameter: scores are normalized to [0, 1] with arctan and each path gets a weight in [0, 1]. Bruch et al. found weighted fusion beats RRF with a small labeled set.
What is the difference between hybrid and vector search, and does hybrid search always outperform vector-only search?
Not on every query: Microsoft measured BM25 alone at 79.2 vs hybrid 61.0 on keyword-only queries. Compare dense-only, BM25-only and hybrid on your own queries with recall@k or NDCG before you choose.
Can I use hybrid search from LangChain or LlamaIndex?

Yes. langchain-milvus adds BM25BuiltInFunction to the Milvus vector store with weighted or RRF ranking, and LlamaIndex has a full-text search guide for Milvus. Both call the same hybrid_search underneath.
